purpose: Re-express the bounded-occurrence SAT frontier as one explicit hard degree constraint inside the 2026 subcubic general-factor dichotomy, so every other locally tractable ingredient can be separated from the only universal hard atom.

construction.input: A CNF with clauses of size 2 or 3 and each variable occurring at most three times, obtained by a polynomial Tovey-style normalization.
construction.graph: Build a subcubic graph with one variable vertex per Boolean variable, one clause vertex per clause, and one degree-2 inverter vertex for every negative literal occurrence.
construction.variable_constraint: If variable x has d occurrence branches, assign degree constraint {0,d}. Degree 0 encodes x=0 and degree d encodes x=1, forcing all variable-side occurrence bits equal. The only hard case is d=3, i.e. {0,3}.
construction.positive_literal: Connect the variable branch directly to its clause vertex, so the clause-side edge is selected iff x=1.
construction.negative_literal: Subdivide the branch by an inverter vertex with degree constraint {1}; exactly one of the variable-side and clause-side edges is selected, so the clause-side edge is selected iff x=0.
construction.clause_constraint: For a k-clause (k in {2,3}), assign interval degree constraint {1,...,k}; this requires at least one literal-side edge to be selected.
construction.decision_identity: The general-factor instance has a feasible factor iff the CNF is satisfiable. Satisfying assignments map to factors by selecting exactly the literal-side branches made true; feasible factors map back because each variable {0,d} vertex has one global Boolean state and every clause has positive selected degree.
construction.size: The construction is linear in the number of literal occurrences and preserves maximum graph degree at most three.

source_alignment.paper: Shao and Zivny, Real-weighted general factors on subcubic graphs, Mathematical Programming, published 2026-09-14
source_alignment.theorem_use: Their Theorem 1.2 gives a strongly polynomial-time algorithm on subcubic graphs whenever the arity-3 degree constraint {0,3} is absent, while the mixed regime containing {0,3} is the exceptional NP-hard side of the dichotomy.
source_alignment.interpretation: Our exact SAT encoding uses only interval clause constraints, degree-1 inverter constraints, easy {0,d} variable constraints for d<=2, and the single exceptional hard atom {0,3} for irreducible degree-3 variables.

do_not_retry: generic matching reduction that ignores the {0,3} all-or-none constraint
generic subcubic general-factor solver from the tractable side of the dichotomy
local rank-2 replacement that unties the three occurrence bits
anti_loop_consequence.exact_live_atom: ALL_OR_NONE_3 = {000,111} = degree constraint {0,3} on a subcubic variable vertex.

two_tractable_relaxations.fact: Both relaxations lie on the strongly-polynomial side of the Shao-Zivny subcubic theorem, while R1 intersection R2 = {0,3} locally.
two_tractable_relaxations.warning: Solving R1 and R2 separately is not enough. A universal algorithm needs one common factor satisfying both relaxations simultaneously, or an equivalent global augmentation theorem; naive independent optimization loses the shared Boolean state.

next_target.name: E8_GLOBAL_ALL_OR_NONE3_AUGMENTATION_V1_7
next_target.directive: Construct a deterministic polynomial-time common-factor/augmentation algorithm that removes all degree-1/degree-2 defects introduced by the two tractable relaxations and returns a factor with every variable degree in {0,3}, without branching over variables.
success_obligations: arbitrary normalized 2/3-CNF with occurrence degree at most three
no exponential parity split over {0,3} vertices
no hidden exponential oracle, dimension, or bitlength

scientific_ceiling.NEW_EXACT_FRONTIER: Global polynomial elimination of the subcubic all-or-none degree-3 constraint {0,3}.
